title: Midnight Runway — Quarterly Swimlane Grid
description: A dark-ground swimlane roadmap dividing work across four Q-columns and three labeled workstream rows, with pill milestones carrying tri-color status dots and a dashed today-line — built for internal product reviews, not boardroom theater.
philosophy: This template exists for the room where things actually get built: PMs, engineering leads, and design directors who must reconcile competing timelines in a single glance. It refuses decorative hierarchy — every element earns its pixel, from the restrained quarter headers to the tri-color status dots. The midnight ground is deliberate: it recedes so the swimlane structure and milestone pills carry the full cognitive weight. It is not a pitch deck; it is a shared map that a cross-functional team can argue over productively.
goodFor: Internal quarterly product reviews with 2–4 concurrent workstreams
Engineering or PM all-hands where cross-team dependencies need surfacing
Roadmap walkthroughs for VP or C-suite stakeholders who want status at a glance
Slides embedded as screenshots in Notion, Confluence, or Linear
avoidFor: Client-facing pitches where internal roadmap detail must stay confidential
Teams with more than five workstreams — rows compress to an unreadable height
Printed A4 handouts — the dashed today-line and status dots lose fidelity at small scale
Single-initiative status updates that carry no swimlane or cross-stream context
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like stepping into a war-room dashboard moments before a cross-functional review begins — dark, calm, and loaded with latent structure. A barely-visible echo of the quarterly grid floats in the background, implying the machinery behind the cover without exposing it. Composition is left-weighted and asymmetric: the title stakes its ground with restrained confidence while the right field breathes wide open. Avoid decorative flourish entirely — every mark should feel load-bearing, as if the team that built the roadmap also designed the slide.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid; deck title and subtitle anchor left in columns 1–7, leaving the right third as deliberate negative space. A single thin horizontal rule sits below the title block, acting as the sole hierarchy separator. Ghost vertical quarter-column dividers bleed full height edge-to-edge in the background at reduced opacity, planting the swimlane DNA before any content slide appears. Deck metadata — date, team or product line — sits bottom-left flush with the outer margin; no page number on the cover.

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like a war-room operations map — purposeful and slightly austere, built for people reconciling competing timelines without ceremony. The midnight ground recedes entirely, letting the grid scaffolding and glowing pill milestones carry all cognitive weight. Rhythm is dense-modular: equidistant column divisions, uniform row heights, and restrained label treatment create a calm structure beneath which tri-color status signals pop with controlled urgency. Avoid any illustrative or decorative marks — every element must read unambiguously as data, structure, or status.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed 12-column grid: cols 1–2 form a fixed left sidebar carrying workstream row labels, while cols 3–12 hold the swimlane body split into four equidistant Q-column divisions with minimal header labels above the grid boundary. Three horizontal rows of equal height fill the body, separated by hairline rules; milestone pills are placed at timeline-accurate positions within each row. A single vertical dashed rule crosses all three rows as the today-line marker. Slide number sits bottom-right outside the grid; no decorative header band or logo zone intrudes on the swimlane area.
